title: Longest Palindromic Path in Graph
summary: Given an integer n and an undirected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and a 2D array edges indicating connections between nodes, along with a string label where each character corresponds to a node, find the longest path that forms a palindrome by visiting unique nodes.
statement: Given an integer n and an undirected graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and a 2D array edges indicating connections between nodes, along with a string label where each character corresponds to a node, find the longest path that forms a palindrome by visiting unique nodes. You can start at any node and move to any adjacent node, visiting each node at most once.
constraints: The undirected graph has at most 14 nodes.
A path may start anywhere but may visit each node at most once.
Maximize path length whose node labels form a palindrome.
hints: A palindrome can be grown symmetrically from one center node or one equal-label center edge.
Track used-node masks and the two current endpoints.
Extend both endpoints to distinct unused neighbors having equal labels.
Every simple palindromic path reduces to a valid shorter center state after removing its matching endpoint pair.
editorial: Every simple palindromic path reduces to a valid shorter center state after removing its matching endpoint pair.

tests.explanation: No two-node or longer path is palindromic, so the answer is one.
